description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Mozambique Country Programme works to reduce the time, cost, and complexity of trade along the Beira Corridor, a critical transit route linking landlocked Malawi and Zimbabwe to the Port of Beira and onward to regional and global markets. Operating since 2020, the Programme targets three interconnected priorities: improving corridor and border efficiency at key nodes including Beira Port and the Machipanda border crossing through trade facilitation measures and digital customs systems developed in partnership with the Mozambique Revenue Authority; strengthening agricultural export competitiveness by digitising phytosanitary certification through the e-Phyto system, which has reduced certificate processing times from an average of twelve days to two to three, and building private sector and institutional capacity to meet sanitary and phytosanitary standards for value chains such as mango; and promoting inclusive trade with targeted support for women traders at Machipanda, improving their access to trade information, financial services, and formalisation pathways
Maputo is the capital city of Mozambique

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

title.narrative: Average time taken to process e-phyto
Time taken process and issue e-phyto

comment.narrative: 12 days taken to process and issue ephytos
reflects 75% utilization of the e-phytos leading to a time reduction by 5%

91% reduction in average processing time from 12 days to 25 hours following the automation of the phytosanitary certification process which was previously paper-based and manual. The Integrated Export and Import Certification System (IEICS), known as SELICEF, integration framework was developed, and the secondary data centre was upgraded with TMA’s support

title.narrative: Volume of trade for Citrus exports

description.narrative: Volume of trade in Machipanda in metric tonnes

comment.narrative: volume of trade rise through citrus exports, trainings and coaching on GAP for traders and MSMEs

600 tonnes of citrus exports, worth approximately $470,000 by Massingir Citrus company in Mozambique to South Africa allowing entry by the company to the South African market following TMA’s support in pest surveillance.
